newsitem.title: UK: SNOOKER-O'SULLIVAN RACES TO FASTEST MAXIMUM BREAK.
newsitem.headline: SNOOKER-O'SULLIVAN RACES TO FASTEST MAXIMUM BREAK.

text.p: Ronnie O'Sullivan raced to the fastest 147 maximum break in the 21-year history of the world professional snooker championship on Monday.
O'Sullivan took only five minutes 20 seconds to clear the table in the 14th frame of his first round 10-6 win over fellow-Englishman Mike Price.
The world number eight is only the fourth man to make a maximum break in the final stages of the tournament and, unless anyone equals it, will pick up an added prize of 147,000 pounds ($240,000).
The three previous players to make a maximum break were Canadian Cliff Thorburn in 1983, Englishman Jimmy White in 1992 and current world number one Stephen Hendry of Scotland two years ago.
O'Sullivan, 21, made his first century break at the age of 10, registered his first maximum break when he was 15 in a regional tournament and turned professional in 1992.

At the age of 17 he became the youngest winner of an international professional tournament with a victory in Bangkok and was the youngest ever winner of a ranking event when he won the U.K. title by beating Hendry 10-6 in the final at the age of 17 years 11 months.
A jubilant O'Sullivan said afterwards: "I was shaking like a leaf but I didn't want to break the rhythm.
"When I saw how the balls had broken, I just had to go for it and win the frame in one visit. I never went out of position all the way."

O'Sullivan's quickfire style of play has gained him a large following but he has frequently fallen foul of officialdom. He was fined 20,000 pounds ($32,720) and given a two-year suspended ban last year for assaulting an official.
Two years earlier he broke down in tears during a television interview and threatened to quit snooker after losing in the quarter-finals of the U.K. Open.
